summary: Kickoff: incident ownership becomes the key must-have; Go becomes trainable; team, outcomes and two restrictions.

changes.value: Owns production incidents end to end
changes.quote: I want someone who owns production incidents end to end.
Go can be learned on the job.

changes.value: 6 backend engineers, report to the CTO, shared on-call rota
changes.quote: Six backend engineers, they report to me, and everyone is on a shared on-call rota.

changes.value: Owns on-call for the routing service
changes.quote: In six months they own on-call for the routing service.
Within a year they lead a squad of three.

changes.value: Do not approach current Carrio staff (integration partner)
changes.quote: Please do not approach anyone currently at Carrio, they are our integration partner.
ideally I'd like top-10 university graduates.

bias.note: University prestige is a proxy that can exclude people by background; ask whether it is job-related before using it.

study.prompt: Incident ownership is now the key must-have, and Go is trainable. In your own words: how would you tell, in a screening, that someone led an incident rather than just joined it?
points: Asks for one concrete incident they led
Checks what they decided and what changed afterwards (post-mortem, follow-up)
Does not spend the screening on Go details
